input.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
input.rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (14.1) and each Deliverable, with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel (14.2). Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, backed by the perpetual Section 13.2 licence where embedded (14.3), and 14.4 bars joint ownership and keeps feedback unrestricted for us. The 14.1 "improve the Services" processing right is confined to improving the Services for us and is further constrained by Section 15.1 (no model training or cross-customer combination without consent), so it does not transfer rights in our data.

input.quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
input.rationale: Affiliates and contractors are expressly covered (13.1); paid-up and embedded software carries a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence with modification rights (13.2); licence rights transfer to an Affiliate or successor (13.3); and there is no at-will revocation — suspension is limited to a material uncured breach after notice and cure. The Section 13.4 restrictions are conventional and expressly do not limit authorised security testing or use of Customer Data and output.

input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is our walk-away position, and it directly contradicts Section 22.2, which already says Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-based only and with no system access; the Section 22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

input.quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages on us of USD 25,000 per day triggered by any dependency delay, however minor — our walk-away position, since accrual is unbounded and could exceed the remaining contract value. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs, and confirmed no penalties are payable by us.
